messages.author: 467dd42188f7efb4
messages.subject: dplyr::filter question
parts:
I've been really amazed by the speed improvements of the initial dplyr release. 

A question about the behavior of filter, motivated by ranking of SSA baby name data.

bn <- read.csv("http://github.com/hadley/data-baby-names/raw/master/baby-names.csv", header=T)

b.out2 <- tbl_df(bn) %.%
                group_by(year, sex) %.%
                arrange(year, sex, desc(percent)) %.%
                dplyr::mutate(rank = 1:n()) %.%
                filter(rank %in% 1:10 & year >= 1945)

(just as an aside, this takes about 2 seconds on my machine, and the relevant ddply call takes 2:30. that's brilliant!).

when it comes to the b.out2, the following filter operations work as expected

filter(b.out2, year == 1945 &  rank == 1)

Source: local data frame [2 x 5]
Groups: year, sex

  year  name  percent  sex rank
1 1945 James 0.054288  boy    1
2 1945  Mary 0.044054 girl    1

and I can subset as one would with a normal data.frame

b.out2[b.out2$name == "James",][1:4,]

   year  name  percent sex rank
1  1945 James 0.054288 boy    1
21 1946 James 0.052999 boy    1
41 1947 James 0.050987 boy    1
61 1948 James 0.049697 boy    1

but this dplyr::filter operation returns no matches  

filter(b.out2, name == "James")

Source: local data frame [0 x 5]
Groups: year, sex

What am I missing about the proper use of filter?
